purpose: Admission measurement of the full AWR hot path. Targets are provisional engineering thresholds fixed before measurement; they are not relaxed after observing results.
measured_path: Engine.step(handles) end to end, called from Python: active-set canonicalization and validation, budget checks, native compaction, sparse gather, per-window gauge transport, shared frozen 88-parameter HCA, controller, MEAN reconciliation, transactional commit into the volatile pool.
cold_phases_reported_separately: instance window extraction and bulk creation
windows: fixtures.extract_window(seed relation, max_incidences=65536): the seed plus up to 3 relations sharing the most participants; slot roles are a random permutation; seeds drawn without replacement (numpy PCG64, registry seed + 1). Disclosed per registry: participant degree, relation arity, window links, relation binding overlap distributions.
workload: Each iteration activates a fresh uniform random sample of A live instance handles without replacement (numpy PCG64 seeded 118400 + A), generated before timing. Random access over the whole registry is the conservative cache case.
initial_state: Every materialized relation row seeded N(0, 1) per coordinate (PCG64 seed 118500) before warmup.
timer: time.perf_counter_ns immediately around each Engine.step call. Every measured call is recorded, including refused calls; any non-EXECUTED disposition is counted as a failure and keeps its latency in the statistics.
process: One subprocess per registry; Python gc enabled (default); single thread (OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS=1); torch is not imported in measurement processes.
statistics: nearest-rank p50, p95, p99; max; mean; over all measured samples.
admission_rule: HOT_PATH_QUALIFIED only if, for the primary configuration, every registry meets every p95 target with zero failures, the capacity-regression rule holds, and the parity check on the benchmark fixture passes. Otherwise PERFORMANCE_NONQUAL with the bottleneck identified. Secondary configurations are reported, not gating.
capacity_regression_rule: for each A: p95(INST50K) <= 2.0 * p95(SMALL) and p95(STRESS1M) <= 2.0 * p95(SMALL)
memory: peak RSS (getrusage ru_maxrss) after cold construction and after measurement; Registry.nbytes, AWRState.nbytes, engine scratch bytes.
allocations: separate untimed run of 200 primary steps per A under tracemalloc: transient peak traced bytes above the pre-step baseline (mean, max), net retained bytes per step, and net live Python blocks per step (sys.getallocatedblocks). tracemalloc cannot count freed transient allocations, so a total allocation count is not claimed. The native kernel performs no heap allocation (stack buffers only; preallocated engine scratch).
full_population_sweep: INST50K and STRESS1M: one synchronous step over all 50,000 instances with a sweep-sized budget; 2 warmup + 10 timed repeats; reported separately and never as hot-path latency.
parity_on_benchmark_fixture: STRESS1M: 3 active sets of 64 drawn from the measured workload; native vs simple reference after one pass must be <= 1e-12.
oracle_baseline: torch oracle adapter on SMALL, A=64, R114, 1 pass: 3 warmup + 20 timed steps (justification baseline for the native backend, not a candidate).
nonclaims: Latency qualification is not scientific qualification; R93 ENERGY_NORMALIZED_DENOMINATOR_HOLD is unaffected.
Measured on the session host only; other hardware is not characterized.
